statement.text:
A system of additive subgroups σij , 1 ⩽ i, j ⩽ n, of a field K is called a net
(or a carpet) of order n if σir σrj ⊂ σij for all i, r, j. A net that does not contain
the diagonal is called an elementary net. A net σ = (σij ) is said to be irreducible if
all σij are nontrivial. An elementary net σ is said to be closed if the elementary net
subgroup E(σ) does not contain additional elementary transvections.
    Let R be a principal ideals domain with 1 ∈ R, let k be the field of fractions
of R, and K an algebraic extension of the field k. Let σ = (σij ) be an irreducible
elementary net σ = (σij ) over K such that all σij are R-modules. Is the net σ closed?
                                                                            V. A. Koı̆baev
